Rajgrod Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Rajgród, Poland

Not demolished. Rajgród's Jews, first recorded at the end of the 16th century, made up 54 percent of the town by 1897, most later murdered between 1941 and 1942, including during a local pogrom in June 1941 and at Treblinka. This cemetery's earliest mention dates to 1719, and it was the subject of a dispute between Rajgród's Jews and the Chevra Kadisha of Tykocin, documented elsewhere in this collection, whose own burial brotherhood was established in 1747. During WWII, Jewish forced laborers were made to use some tombstones to reinforce roads by German order; others were used to fill the foundation of a water mill administrator's house on the Wojda estate. In 2014, descendants of Rajgród's Jews, working with the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage in Poland, cleaned the site and unveiled a memorial monument — which was then vandalized multiple times between 2014 and 2015.
